name: Suji Halwa
description: Classic Pakistani suji halwa with semolina slowly toasted in ghee, then cooked with warm cardamom syrup until soft, glossy and fragrant.
method: Combine the water, sugar and crushed cardamom in a saucepan and heat until the sugar dissolves. Keep this syrup warm while you toast the semolina.
Melt the ghee in a heavy pan over medium-low heat, add the semolina and stir continuously so it colours evenly rather than catching in patches.
Continue roasting until the semolina develops a golden colour and a nutty aroma; patient roasting gives the finished halwa much of its flavour.
Reduce the heat and carefully add the warm syrup in stages while stirring continuously, as the mixture can bubble and release hot steam.
Keep stirring until the semolina absorbs the liquid, swells and the halwa becomes smooth and begins to leave the sides of the pan.
Taste the texture and stop before it becomes dry, since it will firm slightly as it cools.
Garnish with sliced nuts and the optional raisins and serve warm.
